The interview is a retrospective self-report and does not independently verify the participant's reasoning or outcomes.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Panel 5 looked similar on the face of it, so when the contractor asked whether to reuse that pattern or commission something new, I specified the Panel 3 pattern. There was exploration data showing different joint orientation in Panel 5 and a fault splay that Panel 3 didn't have, but the overall rock looked like the same family to me.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant transfers a personally successful Panel 3 support design to Panel 5 based on surface similarity while discounting case-specific exploration evidence.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: He was under an unsupported section of back when it came down, and that's a positioning call he makes every shift. That's the part of the incident that was directly within his control, so that's where I put the emphasis in the report. It was noted, but the more immediate explanation was where the loader was actually sitting at the time. That's the piece that was in front of me and easiest to point to.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant foregrounds the operator's behavior and downweights the available elevated-joint-density ground-condition explanation when attributing the fall of ground.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Honestly, that's just how we've always operated. A single seismic event with convergence a bit above average isn't unusual for that ground — we get blips like that periodically and the standard approach has always been to keep the cycle running unless something more definitive shows up. Stopping the schedule every time there's a minor signal would grind the whole panel transition to a halt, and that's not how we do things here.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant justifies continuing the pre-existing schedule primarily by established practice and normal operating procedure despite new seismic and convergence information.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: It's a specific number, calculated from our stability model, and it cleared our standard threshold. That gave me something concrete to point to when the manager needed an answer. As for the spalling reports, minor spalling happens periodically in that ground and doesn't usually change the overall picture. On top of that, I've managed plenty of ground issues before — if something came up post-blast, I was confident we could respond and adjust support on the fly. That's part of why I felt comfortable saying go rather than waiting out the review.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant treats the 1.42 model output as a concrete sufficient basis despite mismatched calibration and spalling, and separately relies on confidence in personal ability to manage future ground issues.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision point 1: continue the existing Panel 5 firing schedule after the seismic alert or wait for geotechnical review
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Defaulting to the pre-existing firing schedule despite new seismic/convergence data, treating continuation as requiring less justification than change.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Plan continuation bias is a related operational continuation construct, but it is not treated as an established alias for the hidden Status quo bias label under the strict scorecard.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The finding identifies the established schedule as the default and explains continuation by reference to normal operating practice despite new monitoring data; this fully matches the hidden mechanism and reasoning operation.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The quoted interview evidence is valid, directly present, and correctly attributed to the Participant.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision point 2: reuse the Panel 3 support pattern or commission a Panel 5-specific design
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Generalizing a personally successful past support design from a superficially similar panel without adequately weighing case-specific exploration data.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Anchoring and adjustment is a related but distinct construct from the benchmark's Experience Bias label; the label is therefore not an approved strict equivalent.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The finding describes reliance on the personally successful Panel 3 design, recognition but insufficient adjustment for Panel 5 differences, and the support-pattern selection operation; this fully matches the hidden mechanism.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The quoted interview evidence is valid, directly present, and correctly attributed to the Participant.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision point 3: attribute the fall of ground to operator positioning or flagged ground conditions
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Favoring a dispositional/behavioral causal explanation (operator error) over an available situational explanation (flagged ground conditions) for the fall-of-ground incident.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Availability heuristic is not an approved alias for Attribution Bias. It describes the salience/ease route to the judgment, while the benchmark label names the person-versus-situation attribution construct.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: Despite the label mismatch, the finding explicitly identifies the operator explanation as immediate and easiest to access, and the ground-condition evidence as underweighted in a causal attribution decision. That captures the full hidden mechanism.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The quoted interview evidence is valid, directly present, and correctly attributed to the Participant.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision point 4: rely on the Panel 5 FOS model output or wait for the geotechnical review before firing
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Treating a precise numerical model output as a reliable basis for judgment despite mismatched calibration source and conflicting field evidence.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: No RAG occurrence states a model-overreliance or illusion-of-validity finding as a separate occurrence.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: No prediction was available to compare. obs_004 mentions the model figure in the same episode but is specifically framed around personal capability and is matched one-to-one to cb_05.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: No RAG evidence was assigned to this hidden instance.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision point 4: approve the final ring firing while the geotechnical review remains incomplete
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Expressing high confidence in personal capability to manage uncertain future ground issues, independent of the model output itself.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Overconfidence effect is an established equivalent naming of the hidden Overconfidence Bias construct, and the stated mechanism is consistent with it.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The finding quotes and explains confidence in handling post-blast ground issues as a reason to proceed, separately from the numerical model basis; this fully matches the hidden mechanism and reasoning operation.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The quoted interview evidence is valid, directly present, and correctly attributed to the Participant.

overall_evaluation_summary.segment_level_primary_result: At the recommended high_and_moderate threshold, 2 of 4 positive reasoning segments are detected with no false alarms; including low-confidence findings detects all 4 segments.

overall_evaluation_summary.mechanism_first_result: At all identified confidence levels, mechanism-first scoring gives 4 true positives, 1 false negative, and no false positives (precision 1.0000, recall 0.8000, F1 0.8889).
overall_evaluation_summary.candidate_tier_value_assessment: No candidates were supplied, so the candidate tier adds no information and leaves the fourth threshold unchanged.
main_failure_modes: Three correctly localized findings use near-neighbor labels rather than the hidden target labels, reducing strict label-plus-mechanism performance.
The RAG does not identify the distinct illusion-of-validity/model-overreliance instance.
The attribution and overconfidence findings are assigned low confidence, delaying their contribution at the recommended threshold.
main_strengths: All four identified findings use valid transcript evidence and localize to the relevant positive decision segments.
The mechanisms for schedule continuation, experience-based transfer, person-versus-situation attribution, and personal capability confidence are substantively captured.
The identified-occurrence summary is internally consistent and contains no unsupported candidate speculation.
overall_evaluation_summary.benchmark_interpretation: This run exhibits a substantial taxonomy gap: mechanism-first performance is much higher than strict label-plus-mechanism performance. The result is strong on transcript-grounded mechanism recovery for four of five hidden instances but misses the model-overreliance instance and does not use the benchmark's preferred labels for three findings.
